schedule_gaps.detail: GIT DATA LOSS, NOT A MISSED-CYCLE GAP: this 9/24 run found that the live dashboard artifact (published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/be815ca0-0271-47ea-86d3-3e482f34e91c) reflected trading activity through 2026-09-23T20:07:50Z -- including 4 real trades on 9/21 (USO trim, AMD trim, MSFT add) and 9/22 (META initiation) -- that were completely absent from the git repository, whose data/*.json files were still frozen at the 9/18 20:09:38Z state. This means prior runs across 9/19-9/23 (roughly 15 cycles) DID execute, research, and successfully publish the dashboard, but their 'git add / commit / push' step (Step 10) silently failed or was skipped every single time in that window, and since each run's container is ephemeral, that uncommitted work would have been lost forever if the live dashboard hadn't independently retained it. This 9/24 run recovered the missing 4 transactions and 15 history/research-log entries by parsing the live dashboard's embedded JSON (read via the Artifact tool's publish-conflict safeguard, which refused this run's first publish attempt because it had a newer, unseen version) and cross-checked the recovered transaction chain against the recovered ledger snapshot -- it reconciles exactly (cash and quantities match to the cent/4-decimal). The merged data is now committed. RECOMMENDATION: investigate why `git push` (or the commit step before it) was failing for every cycle in this window -- e.g. check for auth/credential expiry, a branch-protection or conflict issue, or a change in the execution environment around 9/18-9/19 -- since this failure mode is silent from the dashboard's perspective (STATUS.dashboard_publish showed 'ok' throughout) and would not have been caught without this reconciliation. Consider adding a git-push-verification step (e.g. checking `git log` post-push, or comparing local HEAD to `git ls-remote`) to the run procedure so a future silent failure surfaces immediately rather than accumulating for days.
